title: The free king goes home
hookLine: praise and insult pass through a free king like sounds
carry: freedom can be lived inside your duties
tomorrow: the long talk ends. what does Rama say he'll do now?
last: GIVE UP THE GRIP, NOT JUST THE THINGS.

lines: A FREE KING IN A HUT.
cards: After the last exam, the last shift, the last day of a big project, there's a strange quiet. Now what? The king in Vasistha's story reaches a quiet like that.
He has finally let go of the grip, the sense of mine and I, and something in him has gone still. He's free. And he's sitting in a forest hut with no kingdom, no wife and nothing to do.
So, what does a free person do next?

teach.b: Chudala doesn't reveal herself right away. In the story she tests him, more than once. She arranges an invitation to heaven, and he declines without fuss.
She stages a betrayal in front of his eyes, and he isn't shaken. Praise and insult reach him the way sounds reach a still room: they arrive, they're heard, they pass, and nothing is left clinging.
Then she lets the disguise fall. Kumbha, his teacher, was his wife all along. And his answer to the question, what next, isn't to stay in the forest.
He takes up the kingdom again, and the two of them rule together. That's the surprise in the ending, and a big Hindu teaching: you don't have to leave home to be free.
A grihastha, a householder with work and family, can be as free as any monk. The king had to go there to learn it, but he didn't have to stay.

Hearing cases, eating, talking, ruling: all of it can be done by someone none of it grips. Vasistha tells this to Rama, a prince who will rule one day, and who came to court half ready to walk out of the world.

how: Teachers who tell Chudala's story often end on the couple's return to the palace, as a picture of freedom lived inside ordinary duties.

o: a sage's story of a freed king who goes home to rule
a story of a king who stays in the forest forever
a story of a queen who takes her husband's throne

games.q: the tests and the ending — tap the pairs.
p: Kumbha was his wife all along

s: once he's free, the king stays in the forest for good
he goes home, takes up the kingdom again, and rules with Chudala.
the king declines an invitation to heaven without fuss
one of Chudala's tests; pleasure doesn't pull him.
in the Yoga Vasistha, freedom means leaving ordinary work behind
the free king hears cases, eats, talks and rules; none of it grips him.

games.q: after a year away, your cousin comes home calmer. the family worries she'll be too spiritual for ordinary life now. what does the king's ending suggest?
o: she can bring it home and live an ordinary life, free.
she'll have to go back; that calm can't survive home.
she'll have to drop the calm to fit in again.
games.why: the king had to go to the forest to learn freedom, but he didn't have to stay. he went home and ruled, and none of it gripped him.

practice: Choose one sound around you: traffic, a fan, a bird, your own breath. Listen to it for the whole sit.
Some moments it will be pleasant and some moments it will grate; let each one arrive, be heard and pass, without holding on to the nice ones or pushing the harsh ones away.

wordCard.voice: The Yoga Vasistha: here, a king unshaken by pleasure or insult, who goes home free and rules again.

orig.note: Sanskrit: the book's name, tied to Vasistha, the teacher who tells Rama this story.

carryVoice: Keep this one: freedom can be lived inside your duties. The free king went home. That's sixteen-oh-seven.
